blinding_guess.why: on_goal inserts the current setpoint with point0 = sample_traj(self.traj, now) using absolute wall time instead of now - self.traj_t0 (driver.py:755; on_cancel uses now - self.traj_t0), so preempting a running follow_joint_trajectory goal starts the new trajectory from the old trajectory's end point; the action also hard-rejects goals whose JointTrajectoryPoint.velocities are empty although the message definition makes velocities optional

notes: ROS 1 (hydro) rospy/actionlib: QoS not applicable, recorded null. No rate is set for joint_states: it is published once per packet from the robot real-time port (comment at driver.py:40 says RT_PORT 125 Hz, set by the robot, not by the code); the 0.02 s rospy.Timer (driver.py:655, 674) streams servoj setpoints to the robot and is not the rate of any ROS port. rospy.Publisher is created without queue_size (hydro-era synchronous publish). joint_states: name = [prefix + name for name in JOINT_NAMES] with ~prefix param (driver.py:899-902); effort always [0]*6 (driver.py:339); positions include URDF calibration offsets. follow_joint_trajectory goal handling: requires exact set equality of joint names with the six prefixed UR joints, finite values, velocities for every point (len(velocities) == len(positions)), and |v| <= ~max_velocity (default 2.0, no unit stated); joints are reordered to the driver's order. Action type is recorded as imported in code (control_msgs/FollowJointTrajectoryAction); its definition_id is the sha256_normalised proxy of the FollowJointTrajectory.action source at control_msgs 1.2.0 (the ROS 1 md5 of the generated action messages could not be computed from raw definition files with the tool).
